analyst.summary: Canara HSBC Life Insurance's core growth metrics -- new business volumes, premium income, and profitability of new business -- all grew strongly in the latest quarter, which is the right way to judge a life insurer's health. Some of the standard financial ratios used in this screening process do not fit an insurance company's business model well, which is likely why this stock scored poorly on that basis. Given the genuinely strong underlying growth, we see this as a hold, while noting we do not have a reliable measure of whether the share price itself is cheap or expensive relative to the company's embedded value.
